svg.text: Air quality: the AQI, health, monitoring, control technologies and regulation

AQI measures the concentrations of pollutants at a place; under 50 is safe outdoors, over 300
is hazardous; children under 18, adults over 65, people with heart or lung disease and
outdoor workers are at highest risk
factors (14.8.1): emission sources; meteorology (wind, temperature, humidity,
inversions); natural events (wildfires, dust storms); seasonal changes
PM (2.5 to 10 micrometres): inflames and irritates airways: asthma, bronchitis
NO2 and SO2: short-term irritation; long-term infections, asthma, bronchitis
main health risks (14.10.1)
respiratory disease: ozone, PM, NO2 trigger asthma; chronic cough, pneumonia
cardiovascular disease: inflammation, vessel damage, high blood pressure, stroke
cancer: PM and carcinogens such as benzene cause lung cancer
reproductive and developmental effects: fertility, premature birth
effects are acute or chronic, depending on pollutant, concentration, exposure, susceptibility
nephelometer: measures PM (dust, smoke, mist, fumes) by the light it scatters
CEMS: continuous emission monitoring of CO, O3, SO2, NO2, VOCs, PM at industrial sites
AQMS: fixed stations with sensors and analysers in cities and industrial zones
remote sensing: satellites measure pollutants over regions and the globe
testing a hypothesis (14.12, 14.13): state it (PM2.5 and NO2 higher at peak traffic), design
(busy roads versus residential sites, variables, instruments), collect data at rush and non-rush
hours, analyse concentrations and trends, interpret for health and policy
catalytic converter: CO to CO2, NOx to N2, hydrocarbons to CO2 and H2O
diesel particulate filter: captures and stores soot from diesel exhaust
selective catalytic reduction: NOx to N2, CO and HC to CO2 and water
over catalysts such as TiO2 and zeolites (diesel engines)
scrubbers: liquids such as water remove PM, SO2, HCl, NH3 and VOCs
from industrial exhaust gases
plus renewable energy, cleaner fuels (CNG, LPG, low-sulfur diesel)
laws in Pakistan: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act (PEPA 1997); National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS); Punjab Environmental Protection (Amendment) Act 2012
measures: vehicle emission standards and cleaner fuels (CNG, LPG); industrial emission control; public awareness and public transport; green belts and
urban planning; smog control (crop-residue burning bans, smog towers); no open burning of waste; low-sulfur diesel
economic: lost productivity, crop damage, corroded infrastructure. social: children, elderly and poor hit hardest; lower quality of life; migration.
political: regulation versus economic interests; pollution crosses borders, so international cooperation is needed; a multi-faceted balance is required
